english.title: Onwardly disclose personal information disclosed by Revenue and Customs under sections 35, 36 or 38
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) having received personal information **(..GIVE DETAILS OF INFORMATION..) that was disclosed by Revenue and Customs under sections 35, 36 or 38 of the Digital Economy Act 2017, further disclosed that information
english.legislation: Contrary to section 42(1) and (3) of the Digital Economy Act 2017 and section 19(4) of the Commissioners for Revenue and Customs Act 2005.

english.notes:
(i) Subsection 42(4) gives the defence for a person charged with an offence under this section.
(ii) This section does not apply to a disclosure which is made with the consent of the Commissioners for His Majesty's Revenue and Customs (which may be general or specific).
(iii) Section 10 of the Interpretation Act 1978 states that any reference to the Sovereign reigning at the time of the passing of the Act is to be construed, unless the contrary intention appears, as a reference to the Sovereign for the time being. As such, references to ‘Her Majesty’ and ‘the Queen’ have been replaced in the wording of the notes above to state ‘His Majesty’ or ‘the King’, although this may not be the strict wording of the legislation.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: maximum 12 months imprisonment and/or fine
INDICTMENT: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or fine

Time limit for prosecutions
None

Note
In the application to an offence committed before the coming into force of section 154(1) of the Criminal Justice Act 2003, the reference to 12 months is to be read as a reference to 6 months.
